newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mandela has not asked for Xanana release-Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Mandela has not asked for Xanana release-Indonesia.

text.p: Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono said on Wednesday South African President Nelson Mandela did not ask for the release of jailed East Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao during his visit to Jakarta earlier this month.
"President Mandela has never touched on in any way, directly or indirectly, the subject of freeing Xanana," Murdiono told reporters.

Mandela, once the world's most famous political prisoner, was reported by Portuguese media at the weekend to have asked Indonesia to free Gusmao, who is serving a 20-year sentence for resisting Indonesian rule in East Timor.

Murdiono added, however, that Mandela had asked for and received permission from President Suharto to meet Xanana to help find a solution to problems of East Timor, a former Portuguese colony annexed by Indonesia in 1976.
"The President (Suharto) saw Mandela's wish (to meet Xanana) as helping settle the East Timor issue internationally," he said.
Mandela has said he is not trying to usurp the role of the United Nations, which has been brokering so far unsuccessful talks between Portugal and Indonesia on the future of East Timor.

But he met Gusmao's spokesman in exile, joint Nobel Peace Prize winner Jose Ramos-Horta, after his return from Indonesia and was scheduled to hold talks on East Timor with Portuguese President Jose Sampaio in Pretoria later on Wednesday.
